title: A code item's land finishes in one run: when its merge request merged and removed code/ID right after the push, land finds the merge on the integration main and goes on to the second pass
goal: land finds the merge of code/ID on the integration main when the branch is already gone from the remote after the push, so the first pass ends with that merge to wait for and the same run goes on to its second pass; land stops with no tip only when neither the branch nor its merge is there

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_land
from pathlib import Path
t = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
env = dict(os.environ, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="a", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="a@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="a",
           GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="a@example.com", GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="/dev/null", GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM="/dev/null")
def g(*a, cwd=t):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
g("init", "-q", "--bare", "remote.git")
g("clone", "-q", "remote.git", "work")
w = t / "work"
g("checkout", "-q", "-b", "main", cwd=w)
(w / "f").write_text("x")
g("add", "f", cwd=w)
g("commit", "-q", "-m", "c", cwd=w)
g("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/main", cwd=w)
# a code/ST-aaaaaaaa merge request merged and removed its branch before land fetched it: main holds its merge commit
g("checkout", "-q", "-b", "code/ST-aaaaaaaa", cwd=w)
(w / "g").write_text("y")
g("add", "g", cwd=w)
g("commit", "-q", "-m", "d", cwd=w)
g("checkout", "-q", "main", cwd=w)
g("merge", "-q", "--no-ff", "-m", "Merge branch " + chr(39) + "code/ST-aaaaaaaa" + chr(39) + " into " + chr(39) + "main" + chr(39), "code/ST-aaaaaaaa", cwd=w)
g("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/main", cwd=w)
g("branch", "-q", "-D", "code/ST-aaaaaaaa", cwd=w)
merged = bl_land.pushed_tip(w, "origin", "code/ST-aaaaaaaa")
none = bl_land.pushed_tip(w, "origin", "code/ST-bbbbbbbb")
print("merged branch gone:", merged, "| never pushed:", none)
ok = bool(merged) and g("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=w) in merged and none is None
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

clauses.clause: land finds the merge of code/ID on the integration main when the branch is already gone from the remote after the push, so the first pass ends with that merge to wait for and the same run goes on to its second pass
land stops with no tip only when neither the branch nor its merge is there

notes: Likely cause, not proven: kg_sync.push_options sends merge_request.auto_merge and merge_request.remove_source_branch, so a merge request that merges at once removes code/<id> before land's pushed_tip fetch, which then reports no tip. Also read: land without --wait-merge is two-pass by design (the first pass says so before the push); the repro covers the missing-branch fetch only. SP-ep7ck2ab (2026-11-08/09): about 9 code-lane items, BG-dq3lxnqm the last, ended land's first pass with 'could not fetch code/<id> from origin after the push' because the merge request had already merged and its branch was gone; each needed a second land run. Merged with ST-5l6ldosq (dropped), one fix: pushed_tip (bl_land.py) returns None when the fetch of code/ID finds no remote ref, so LAND_OPS pending stays empty and the first pass ends 'not done yet'. Night baseline (2026-11-08 18:00 to 2026-11-09 13:00 CET): 129 of the 146 land.end rows of lane code were followed by a second pass of the same item, a second run the orchestrator started by hand. Cause (sync sends merge_request.auto_merge and remove_source_branch, so the request merges and removes code/ID before land's fetch): the repro plants a bare remote whose main holds the Merge branch commit of code/ST-aaaaaaaa and no such branch, and asks pushed_tip for that branch (expects a list holding main's tip) and for a never-pushed branch (expects None); on the base both give None. Keep pushed_tip's signature: kj_land.py and kj_exec.py (SP-lwkdljxg's files) call pending_merge, not pushed_tip, and are not touched here. The fix may read the merge by its subject (Merge branch 'code/ID') on the fetched integration main.
